title: Stop a clean relaunch warning about a session that isn't running, and name the branch on a fresh repository

history.detail:
FAIL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 38, round 1. Audited commit b49fbcf (on e573e96, the sprint start). The sprint file was read fresh at HEAD and is unchanged since e573e96. Verdict: FAIL. Two demonstrated defects, both the same shape: a check that could not actually run is reported as a definite answer. Both fixes are small. All defects are listed here so there is one fix round.

1. [HIGH] Req 1a: isPidAlive() returns false ("positively confirmed gone") when ps is present but cannot answer, which silences the NOTE for a session that is still running.
 - Code (scripts/launcher/role-claims.js, isPidAlive): after process.kill(pid, 0) has already SUCCEEDED, i.e. the process exists, it runs ps -o stat= -p <pid> and does "if (ps.status !== 0 || !stat) return false; // gone by the time ps checked". A ps that exits non-zero for any reason other than the pid being gone is read as "gone".
 - Real-world trigger, shown directly: BusyBox ps (Alpine, and many slim containers and devcontainers) does not support -p. In a real alpine container, docker run --rm --entrypoint sh public.ecr.aws/supabase/vector:0.53.0-alpine -c 'sleep 30 & P=$!; ps -o stat= -p $P; echo exit=$?' prints BusyBox usage text and "ps exit=1 for live pid 7".
 - End-to-end repro of the real code at b49fbcf (macOS). A PATH shim ps reproduces BusyBox's behaviour (usage on stderr, exit 1). Spawn a real sleep 30, then:
   - process.kill(pid,0) says running: true.
   - isPidAlive(pid) returns false.
   - roleClaimWarning('Master Controller', {pid}) returns null, so no NOTE is printed for a previous session that is demonstrably still running.
 - This is exactly the dangerous direction Sprint 25 and Req 1a exist to prevent: "a check that cannot be performed on this platform ... the NOTE fires as it does today", and the acceptance criterion says "every undeterminable branch falls through to the NOTE".
 - Fix: when kill(pid,0) succeeded but ps did not return a usable STAT, do not return false. Re-probe kill(pid,0): ESRCH means false (genuinely gone in between); anything else means null. Add a launcher_test case with a PATH-shimmed failing ps against a live process asserting the NOTE still fires.

2. [MEDIUM] Req 2: branch_state() reports "(not a git repository)" for a real repository whenever git refuses to run.
 - Code (scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py, branch_state): "if repo_check.returncode != 0 or repo_check.stdout.strip() != 'true': return ('no-repo', None)". Every non-zero exit from git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree becomes the specific claim "not a git repository".
 - Req 2 says the undeterminable cases "must not claim any of the three specific cases above".
 - Repro at b49fbcf, in a real clone (.git present, git log works): GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 (git's own hook for its safe.directory ownership check). git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree then exits 128 with "fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at ...", and branch_state() returns ('no-repo', None), so tree_description() prints ".../s38 (not a git repository)".
 - Real trigger: a repository owned by a different OS user than the one running git. That is common on Windows (created elevated, or on a VM shared folder), which is one of this sprint's two workshop platforms. An attendee would be told their repo isn't a repo, and told to run git init in a directory that already has one.
 - Fix: only claim "no-repo" when git positively says so (stderr "not a git repository", or exit 0 with stdout "false" for a non-work-tree). Treat any other failure as ("unknown", None). Add a smoke case using GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 asserting the output does NOT say "not a git repository".

WHAT IS FINE.
 - Req 1: the claim records the launcher's own pid (process.pid). run-role.js awaits spawnClaude for the whole session, so the launcher pid is alive exactly as long as the session. It is recorded before the fail() preflight paths, so a launcher that fails early leaves a dead pid, which is correct.
 - Suppression happens only on an exact === false. A missing or invalid pid returns null, so the NOTE fires. EPERM returns true. Both are correct.
 - On Dev Team's zombie question: the approach is sound. kill(pid,0) cannot see a zombie, and ps STAT Z is the right discriminator on POSIX. The only defect is the failure fallthrough in item 1.
 - On the pty-close measurement: a real pty.fork with the master closed is a faithful reproduction of a terminal disposing its pty (process-group SIGHUP reaching both processes), and it is measured, not argued. It is a stand-in for VS Code's trash can, not VS Code itself; LiveQA's live criteria cover the real thing.
 - The targeted-SIGKILL residual is named honestly.
 - 1c: an old-format record (no pid) returns null, so the NOTE fires. Tested.
 - A grep of the diff for "nobody else"/"nobody is working" finds no such output or comment; the existing NOTE wording is unchanged.
 - Req 2: symbolic-ref --short HEAD resolves an unborn branch and fails on a detached HEAD, which then correctly falls to unknown. Every tree_description() call site gets the new text; nothing is special-cased. The stderr [sprint_lifecycle] banner is untouched (no banner lines in the diff). current_branch() has no remaining callers.
 - Smoke asserts printed text for no-repo, unborn (a real git init with no commits), named, and detached.
 - Req 3: npm view fully-completely version returns 0.2.11 and package.json is 0.2.12; the CHANGELOG entry is present and accurate.
 - Req 4: QA1 ran both suites at b49fbcf in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0. pyflakes is clean.
 - Diff confinement: exactly role-claims.js, sprint_lifecycle.py, launcher_test.js, smoke_test.sh, package.json and CHANGELOG.md, all on the allowed list; run-role.js is untouched, correctly.

FOR LIVEQA, not a finding here. Windows is unmeasured in this build, and run-role.js's own orphan-guard comment says the guard is POSIX-only and claude runs as a grandchild of cmd.exe on Windows. If a Windows trash-can or Terminate All ever kills the node launcher but leaves claude running, the recorded pid reads as gone and the NOTE is suppressed while a session is live. The F6 report's Get-Process observation suggests claude does die on that path, but LiveQA's per-step Get-Process check is what actually settles it. Check claude's state, not only the launcher's.

REQUIRED BEFORE PASS: fix items 1 and 2, each with a test that fails on b49fbcf.

PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 38, round 2. Audited commit a21fcbd (HEAD). The sprint file was re-read and is byte-identical to e573e96, so the requirements have not moved. This round reviews b49fbcf..a21fcbd against the two round-1 findings, on top of the round-1 review of everything else. Verdict: PASS.

1. isPidAlive and an unusable ps (HIGH): FIXED, and demonstrated fixed.
 - Every ps failure path (a throw, ps.error, or a non-zero exit or empty STAT) now goes through reprobeAfterUnusablePs(). That re-runs process.kill(pid, 0) and returns false only on a fresh ESRCH, null otherwise. A genuine exit in the window between the two probes still reads as gone; a ps that cannot answer never does.
 - The zombie path (STAT starting with Z means false) is unchanged.
 - QA1's own repro, re-run at a21fcbd with the same BusyBox-shaped PATH shim ps (usage on stderr, exit 1). QA1 confirmed real BusyBox behaves this way in an alpine container last round.
   - Live sleep process: isPidAlive gives null, and roleClaimWarning PRINTS the NOTE.
   - The same process SIGKILLed and reaped: isPidAlive gives false, and the NOTE is suppressed. So the fix did not break the positive-gone case.
 - Falsification: QA1 swapped b49fbcf's role-claims.js into a clone at a21fcbd and ran launcher_test.js. The new test "a ps that cannot answer (BusyBox's own shape) must NOT be read as process gone for a genuinely running process" FAILS on the old code and passes on the fix.

2. branch_state and a real repository git refuses (MEDIUM): FIXED, and demonstrated fixed.
 - "no-repo" is now returned only when git exits 0 printing something other than "true", or exits non-zero with stderr containing "not a git repository". Every other failure is ("unknown", None).
 - QA1's repro, re-run at a21fcbd: GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 in a real clone gives ('unknown', None) and "(branch unknown)". It no longer claims "not a git repository".
 - A genuinely empty non-repo directory still gives ('no-repo', None).
 - Falsification: with b49fbcf's sprint_lifecycle.py swapped in, smoke_test.sh FAILS on the new assertion. It printed "No sprints yet in ... (not a git repository)" for the dubious-ownership repo, and passes on the fix.
 - Advisory, not a finding: the stderr match is English-only. Under a non-English git locale, a genuine non-repo would degrade to "(branch unknown)". That is the permitted wording for undeterminable cases and never a false specific claim, so Req 2 still holds. Setting LC_ALL=C (or LANG=C) in that subprocess's env would make the positive case locale-independent, which is worth doing in a later sprint if Windows attendees run localized git.

EVERYTHING FROM ROUND 1 STILL HOLDS AT a21fcbd.
 - Req 1/1a/1c:
   - The launcher records its own pid, which stays alive for the whole awaited session.
   - Suppression happens only on an exact === false; a missing, invalid or old-format pid gives null, so the NOTE fires.
   - There is no "nobody else is working here" wording anywhere.
 - 1b: the measurements (macOS kill/ESRCH, the zombie visible only via ps STAT, pty-close taking down launcher and child) are recorded next to the code, naming platform and shutdown path. Windows is explicitly named as unmeasured, and LiveQA's criteria re-confirm it live.
 - Req 2/2a:
   - An unborn branch is named via symbolic-ref; a detached HEAD gives unknown.
   - Every tree_description() call site gets the text; nothing is special-cased.
   - The stderr banner is untouched.
   - Printed text is asserted for no-repo, unborn (a real git init), named, detached and dubious-ownership.
 - Req 3: package.json is 0.2.12 against published 0.2.11 (npm view), and the CHANGELOG entry is present.
 - Diff confinement: role-claims.js, sprint_lifecycle.py, launcher_test.js, smoke_test.sh, package.json, CHANGELOG.md, plus docs/sprints bookkeeping. All on the allowed list.

REQ 4. QA1 ran both suites at a21fcbd in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0. pyflakes is clean.

FOR LIVEQA, carried from round 1. On Windows, after the trash can or Terminate All, confirm claude itself is gone via Get-Process, not only the launcher. run-role.js's orphan guard is POSIX-only; if claude ever outlives the node launcher there, the recorded pid reads as gone and the NOTE would be wrongly suppressed while a session is live.
commit=a21fcbd1627ac7c7429e54ae629f4f976da781b3 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for a21fcbd1627ac7c7429e54ae629f4f976da781b3 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

FAIL: LiveQA live test, sprint 38, round 1. Verdict: FAIL.
One confirmed defect: Req 1's positive case fails live after a normal FC: Start All. Windows was NOT run (the user was unavailable at the VM); no PASS is claimed for Windows. Everything else runnable on macOS was run.

ENVIRONMENT
macOS 26.6.2 arm64, node v24.21.0, Python 3.14.7, git 2.55.0, VS Code (user-driven GUI). Claude Code 2.1.272, which auto-updated to 2.1.273 mid-run (~14:39 local); every NOTE and pty result below after that time is on 2.1.273. Project: ~/Programming/workshop-test-0212. Scratch: this session's scratchpad s38/. Tools: npx, python3, ps, lsof, a python pty capture (scratchpad ptyprobe.py), and screenshots #81-#92 from the user.

PROVENANCE (from the registry)
- npm dist-tags latest 0.2.12. npm view fully-completely@0.2.12 gives gitHead a21fcbd1627ac7c7429e54ae629f4f976da781b3, equal to last_shipped_commit.
- dist.shasum 3bc2498855f24d50865e17a4423661b2660be1f0 equals the npm pack download.
- All 57 published files are byte-identical to git show a21fcbd:<path> (MISMATCHED 0, NOT-IN-COMMIT 0).
- Non-sprint files changed since 0.2.11: CHANGELOG.md, package.json, scripts/baselines/user-owned-content.json, scripts/launcher/role-claims.js, scripts/launcher_test.js, scripts/smoke_test.sh, scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py.

GUIDE STEP 5 REGRESSION (macOS): PASS
npx fully-completely in a new folder with a clean env and empty npm cache: exit 0, "Installed 0.2.12 (first install)", 53 files, the same Notes and log-in lines as 0.2.10. Folder contents: .claude .gitignore .vscode CLAUDE.md docs scripts templates.

REQ 2 LIVE (macOS): PASS
stderr banner unchanged in every run: "[sprint_lifecycle] repo=<folder> script=<folder>/scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py".
- Before git init: "No sprints yet in /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/workshop-test-0212 (not a git repository)."
- After git init: "No sprints yet in ... (branch: master, no commits yet)."
- After the first commit: "No sprints yet in ... (branch: master)."
- Detached HEAD: "(branch unknown)".
- GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 (git refuses the repo): "(branch unknown)", not "not a git repository".
- git absent from PATH: "(branch unknown)", exit 0.
- German-locale git on a real non-repo (git says "Schwerwiegend: Kein Git-Repository"): "(branch unknown)". This is QA1's English-only advisory; it uses permitted wording and makes no false claim.
- The /sprint-status error path also carries the new text: "No state file for sprint 1 in ... (branch: master)."

GUIDE STEP 6 REGRESSION (macOS): PASS
FC: Start All: all tabs came up (#83 Master Controller, #85 QA1, #92 Dev Team 1: role named, "nothing in flight", correct models).

REQ 1: SHUTDOWN PATHS (macOS): PASS on process state
After the trash can on every tab, and again after "Tasks: Terminate Task > Terminate All Tasks", ps/lsof showed no run-role.js or claude process with cwd workshop-test-0212 from the earlier launches. Only the launchers of the most recent Start All were alive (12:24:03 set, checked at 12:25). Relaunch tabs showed no NOTE above the Claude header (#83 #84 #85). Caution: on macOS the NOTE flashes and is then covered by Claude's full-screen UI (see finding 2), so the tab screenshots alone do not prove its absence. The pty captures below are the reliable evidence.

REQ 1: POSITIVE CASE (macOS): FAIL

(A) A simultaneous FC: Start All loses claim records.
- Start All at 14:50:58 launched six launchers (28247 MC, 28248 DT1, 28249 DT2, 28250 QA1, 28251 Pipeman, 28252 LiveQA; ps plus lsof cwd).
- .claude/role-claims.json at 14:51:20:
  - master-controller pid=21170 (12:29, dead)
  - dev-team-1 pid=28248 (alive)
  - dev-team-2 NO RECORD
  - qa1 pid=20618 (12:27, dead)
  - pipeman pid=20975 (12:28, dead)
  - liveqa pid=28252 (alive)
- Only 2 of 6 new launches kept their record. The earlier Start All (12:24:03) likewise left only pipeman and qa1, while master-controller, dev-team-1, dev-team-2 and liveqa launchers were alive with no record.

(B) Consequence, captured through a pty (launcher output for 4 s, then the probe launcher and its claude were terminated):
- liveqa (control): record 28252 alive, launcher 28252 running. NOTE printed: YES. "NOTE: another LiveQA session was recorded starting at 2026-09-15T21:50:58.326Z in this same tree (session b8ec39ff-8117-43b5-9959-9e800f6e5a34)..."
- pipeman: record 20975 dead, launcher 28251 running (claude resuming the same pipeman session). NOTE printed: NO.
- dev-team-2: no record, launcher 28249 running. NOTE printed: NO.
- qa1 (user run at 14:52:12, launcher 29670): record 20618 dead, launcher 28250 running. Terminal scrollback after quitting shows the command followed directly by "Resume this session with: claude --resume "fc:qa1:workshop-test-0212"", with no NOTE. (The pty control above shows the NOTE is emitted when a live record exists.)

The sprint's own LiveQA criterion "with one agent still running, launch that same role again separately — the NOTE appears" therefore fails for pipeman, dev-team-2 and qa1, and passes only for roles whose record survived (dev-team-1 and liveqa; the user also saw the Dev Team 1 and LiveQA NOTE flash). Every extra launch resumes the same conversation (for example, three concurrent "claude --agent liveqa --resume 0c1b9468..." at 14:39), which is exactly the collision the NOTE exists to surface. This is the Risks & Mitigations item "The fix silences a real collision."

(C) The record loss predates this sprint; the silence is new.
Scratch installs, six launchers started concurrently with claude absent from PATH (each records a claim, then stops at preflight; no sessions):
- 0.2.11: records saved 1, 2, 2 of 6 across three trials.
- 0.2.12: 6, 4, 3 of 6.
- 0.2.12 launched sequentially: 6 of 6.
So concurrent writes to role-claims.json lose entries on both versions. On 0.2.11 a surviving stale record still produced the NOTE (any record warned). On 0.2.12 the stale record's pid is dead, so the NOTE is suppressed while that role's current session runs. The F6 behaviour itself works as designed: a dead record gives no NOTE and a live record gives a NOTE. The defect is that after the attendee's normal flow (FC: Start All launches all roles in the same instant) 3 to 5 of the 6 records do not describe the running session, and the new suppression turns that into silence.
Suggested direction (Dev Team 1 and QA1 decide): make the claim write safe under concurrent launch (serialize or merge-on-write), and add a concurrent-launch test that asserts all six records survive. The current tests launch one role at a time.

OTHER FINDINGS (not this sprint's requirements, for Master Controller)
1. Req 1 wording versus intent. Taken literally ("the previously recorded session"), (B) could be argued as conforming, since the recorded session is dead. The sprint's live criterion and risk list make the intent a running same-role session, and that is what fails.
2. On macOS the NOTE, when printed, is visible for well under a second before Claude's full-screen UI replaces it (user report, twice). An attendee cannot read it. On Windows 0.2.10 (guide pass #74) it stayed visible above the header. This probably predates 0.2.12.
3. Probe side effects, disclosed. My probes overwrote the pipeman, dev-team-2, liveqa and (earlier) master-controller records with probe pids that are now dead. No probe process remains. Killing the pipeman probe made Claude Code print "fullscreen renderer didn't finish starting last time ... using the classic renderer" on the next launch.

NOT RUN
Windows: the whole Windows criterion set (Steps 5-6 on the VM, Req 2 output there, trash can and Terminate All with Get-Process claude,node, positive case). The user was not available at the VM this round. QA1's carried question, whether claude outlives the node launcher on Windows after the trash can or Terminate All, is still open. It must be run in the retest.

CONDITIONAL: QA1 live-loop audit, sprint 38, commit 7f71f41. Verdict: CONDITIONAL. The lock fixes exactly what it claims to fix. A second, demonstrated path to the same silencing LiveQA failed on remains, and should be closed in the same fix round rather than found by the retest.

WHAT THIS COVERS. The tree delta from last_shipped_commit a21fcbd to 7f71f41, outside sprint bookkeeping:
 - scripts/launcher/role-claims.js
 - scripts/launcher_test.js
 - package.json
 - CHANGELOG.md
 - scripts/baselines/user-owned-content.json (Pipeman's c7ed3a6 regen for 0.2.12)
The sprint file was re-read and is unchanged since e573e96. LiveQA's round-1 FAIL notes were read in full.

1. The lost-update fix: CORRECT.
 - The read-modify-write in recordRoleClaim sits inside acquireClaimsLock/releaseClaimsLock, with the release in a finally.
 - The lock is fs.openSync(path, 'wx'), which is O_EXCL on POSIX and CREATE_NEW on Windows. A lock older than 10 s is stolen, total wait is capped at 3 s, and a non-EEXIST error or timeout proceeds unlocked. That is no worse than 0.2.12 and never blocks a launch, consistent with "it warns, it never gates".
 - The critical section is milliseconds, so 3 s is ample.
 - Negative control, run by QA1: with acquireClaimsLock forced to return null in a clone at 7f71f41, the new "FC: Start All -- all six roles ... keep their own claim record" test FAILED 3 of 3 runs. With the lock restored, launcher_test.js passed 3 of 3 runs, so the concurrent test is a real regression test and is not flaky.

2. [HIGH] Req 1 positive case, second path: a short duplicate launch overwrites the claim of a session that is still running, so the next launch is silent.
 - The record keeps only the LAST claim per role (claims[roleId] = {...new}). Once any later launch of that role has written and then exited, the next launch reads that dead pid as "the previous session has ended", even though an earlier session of the same role is still live.
 - Demonstrated with real run-role.js processes at 7f71f41 (headless, a stand-in claude on PATH that answers --version and auth status and then sleeps FAKE_SESSION_SECONDS, and FULLY_COMPLETELY_ROLE_CLAIMS_PATH_OVERRIDE set):
   - A: qa1, session sleeps 30 s, in the background.
   - B, 2 s later: qa1, sleeps 1 s. Stderr has the "NOTE: another QA1" line (correct), then B exits 0.
   - C: qa1. A's launcher pid (32064) was confirmed alive via kill -0 during C, yet C's stderr has zero NOTE lines. role-claims.json then holds only C's own claim, having replaced B's dead one.
   - Also reproduced directly against the module (recordRoleClaim/roleClaimWarning with a live sleep 60 pid for A and a short sleep 0.2 pid for B): NOTE false, then true, then false with A alive.
 - Why this is in scope. The sprint's Risks & Mitigations names "The fix silences a real collision" and says Req 1 "requires the NOTE when the previous session is running". LiveQA's live criterion ("with one agent still running, launch that same role again separately -- the NOTE appears") and its round-1 FAIL both read Req 1 as "a running same-role session", and the concurrent-write fix only closes one way of breaking that. The attendee flow that reaches it is ordinary: open a duplicate tab or run Start All twice, notice, close the duplicate, then relaunch or Start All again while the original is still running.
 - On 0.2.11 any surviving record warned. On 0.2.12 and at 7f71f41 this is silence, the same regression class LiveQA failed.
 - If Master Controller rules on LiveQA's open "Req 1 wording versus intent" question that the literal "previously recorded session" reading governs, this becomes a named residual instead of a defect. Until then, the sprint's own risk statement decides it.
 - Suggested fix (Dev Team decides the shape). Per role, keep every claim not POSITIVELY confirmed dead, rather than only the last one:
   - On record, prune only entries where isPidAlive(pid) === false, then append the new claim.
   - Warn if any remaining prior entry is not confirmed dead. Undeterminable still warns, per 1a.
   - Read an old single-object record as a one-element list (1c).
   - Do it inside the existing lock.
 - Test: the A-long / B-short / C sequence above, asserting C prints the NOTE while A is alive and prints none once A has also exited.

3. Baseline table (c7ed3a6): CORRECT. The seven USER_OWNED hashes recomputed from git show a21fcbd:<path> match files[path]["0.2.12"] with 0 mismatches, and npm run baselines:check covers everything through 0.2.12.

4. Version and CHANGELOG. package.json is 0.2.13 against published 0.2.12 (npm view; gitHead a21fcbd = last_shipped_commit). The 0.2.13 "Corrects 0.2.12" entry is present. If item 2 lands in this same fix round, extend the entry to cover it.

5. Tests at 7f71f41 in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, 3 of 3 runs. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0.

ADVISORIES, NOT BLOCKING.
 (a) Stale-lock steal race. Two waiters that both see a lock older than 10 s can both unlinkSync it: A unlinks, A creates its own lock, then B's unlink deletes A's live lock, and both enter. This is reachable only after a holder crashed mid-critical-section and left a lock at least 10 s old. Rare, and the consequence is the pre-fix race, not something new. Checking inode or mtime identity before unlinking, or renaming aside before the steal, would close it.
 (b) A lock left behind by a crash (.claude/role-claims.json.lock) is not in the installer's managed .gitignore block, so git add -A could commit it, which is sprint 36 Req 7's own class of problem. Adding it touches install.js, which is outside this sprint's allowed diff list, so it is Master Controller's call.

FOR LIVEQA'S RETEST, carried forward. Windows was not run in round 1. After the trash can or Terminate All, confirm via Get-Process that claude itself is gone, not only the node launcher (the orphan guard is POSIX-only). Once item 2 is fixed, add the duplicate-then-close-then-relaunch sequence from item 2 to the positive-case checks on both platforms.

REQUIRED BEFORE A LIVE-LOOP PASS: fix item 2 with a test that fails on 7f71f41. | commit=7f71f4171f55cafffb2d5ddb539efbea0fc30a7a

CONDITIONAL: QA1 live-loop audit, sprint 38, commit 07a4b9c. Verdict: CONDITIONAL. The A/B/C fix works. It introduces a demonstrated regression of this sprint's own F6 for every upgraded install, and the stale-lock "fix" does not close the race it claims to.

WHAT THIS COVERS. The tree delta from 7f71f41 (QA1 CONDITIONAL at 6e311d9) to 07a4b9c, outside bookkeeping: scripts/launcher/role-claims.js, scripts/launcher_test.js and CHANGELOG.md. The sprint file was re-read and is unchanged since e573e96.

1. The A/B/C finding from the last audit: FIXED.
 - A role's claims are now a list. recordRoleClaim keeps entries where isPidAlive !== false and appends; roleClaimWarning warns if any entry is not confirmed dead.
 - The new unit and real-subprocess A/B/C tests pass at 07a4b9c.
 - Dev Team 1 reports a negative control (revert to keep-latest, and both fail). QA1 did not re-run it this round, because the round-1 repro shape is what those tests encode.

2. [HIGH] Regression: an old-format (pre-0.2.12, no pid) claim is never pruned, so the NOTE fires on EVERY relaunch forever for any upgraded install, which is F6 itself.
 - Cause: isPidAlive(undefined) returns null (undeterminable), so the filter "isPidAlive(claim.pid) !== false" keeps that entry on every write, and roleClaimWarning warns on it every time.
 - Before this commit, the old record was replaced on the first launch after upgrade, so it warned exactly once.
 - Demonstrated with real run-role.js processes (headless, stand-in claude on PATH, FULLY_COMPLETELY_ROLE_CLAIMS_PATH_OVERRIDE). The planted claims file is {"qa1": {"sessionId": "old-0-2-11-session", "startedAt": "2026-09-10T09:00:00.000Z"}}, the exact 0.2.10/0.2.11 shape. Three sequential relaunches, with no other run of that claims file active:
   - At 07a4b9c: NOTE lines 1, 1, 1. The file afterward still holds the old pid-less entry plus the latest claim.
   - At 7f71f41, same setup: NOTE lines 1, 0, 0.
